name: Benign Tumor of Fallopian Tubes
aliases: Benign Neoplasm of the Fallopian Tube

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Benign Fallopian Tube Tumors

criteria.description: Identification of a well-circumscribed, non-invasive mass localized to the fallopian tube on ultrasound or MRI
Histological confirmation of benign epithelial or stromal tumor without cellular atypia or invasion
Immunohistochemical absence of malignant markers such as p53 overexpression or high Ki-67 proliferation index

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging characteristics consistent with a benign fallopian tube mass plus histopathological confirmation of benign tumor
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of malignancy and other adnexal masses.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable adnexal mass localized to fallopian tube
Localized fallopian tube swelling detected on imaging

common.symptomName: Pelvic discomfort or localized pelvic fullness

occasional.symptomName: Hydrosalpinx formation secondary to tumor obstruction
searchTerms: fluid-filled fallopian tube due to blockage

occasional.symptomName: Urinary frequency due to pelvic mass effect
searchTerms: urinary urgency due to pelvic pressure

rare.symptomName: Acute pelvic pain from tumor torsion
searchTerms: sudden pelvic pain from twisted tumor

laboratory: Normal tumor markers (CA-125 typically normal or mildly elevated)
Absence of inflammatory markers elevation unless secondary infection
imaging: Ultrasound showing well-defined adnexal mass localized to fallopian tube
MRI demonstrating non-invasive, encapsulated lesion without infiltration
Doppler ultrasound may show preserved vascular flow
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations associated
other: Histopathology confirming benign epithelial or stromal tumor

distinguishingFeatures: Malignant histopathology with cellular atypia and invasion
Elevated CA-125 and other tumor markers
Aggressive clinical course with rapid growth
Fluid-filled fallopian tube without solid mass
Often associated with pelvic inflammatory disease history
Absence of solid tumor on imaging
Mass localized to ovary rather than fallopian tube

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of adnexal mass
Unexplained weight loss or systemic symptoms
references: Orphanet: Benign Tumor of Fallopian Tubes - ORPHA:180237
WHO Classification of Tumors of Female Reproductive Organs, 5th Edition
